# Start work in the right directory

## Problem statement

When `wl ampa start-work` provisions and enters a *fresh* dev container, the
interactive shell is started with an explicit `cd` to the container-local
sandbox path (`/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`) instead of the canonical
`/workdir/project` symlink. Any already-claimed container is re-entered with
`cd /workdir/project`, so the initial entry is inconsistent with re-entry,
confuses the shell prompt (it computes its relative path against
`/workdir/project`), and makes tooling or user commands that assume
`/workdir/project` report the wrong location.

## Users

- **AI agents** launched into a container by `wl ampa start-work`: they expect
  the project to be at `/workdir/project` so scripts, prompts and `wl ampa
  finish-work` resolve consistently.
- **Operators** reviewing/spawning sandboxes: they expect the documented
  `/workdir/project` path to hold regardless of whether the container was just
  created or re-entered.

### Example user stories

- As an AI agent, when I am dropped into a fresh dev container, I want to be in
  `/workdir/project` so that relative paths, the prompt and tooling match every
  other entry point.
- As an operator, when I run `wl ampa start-work <id>` and then `pwd`, I want to
  see `/workdir/project`, not a `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl ampa start-work <work-item-id>` (and its `sw` alias) starts the
  interactive shell in `/workdir/project` for a newly-provisioned container,
  i.e. `pwd` inside the container reports `/workdir/project` (verification:
  manual E2E `wl ampa sw <id>` then `pwd`).
- [ ] Initial entry is consistent with the already-implemented re-entry and
  legacy-container paths, which both `cd /workdir/project` (verification: code
  inspection + assertion that all interactive entry commands reference
  `/workdir/project`).
- [ ] The shell prompt's relative-path segment resolves against
  `/workdir/project` (no leading `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_*` shown) and
  `/etc/ampa_bashrc` continues to `cd /workdir/project` (verification: manual
  E2E prompt check).
- [ ] An automated regression test asserts that the interactive entry command
  changes into `/workdir/project` and not the container-local
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` path; the test fails against the
  pre-fix code and passes after the fix (verification: `npm test` /
  `node --test` in the ampa project).
- [ ] Behaviour of `wl ampa finish-work` and the `--wait` / re-entry flows is
  unchanged (verification: existing ampa test suite green).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The container project is physically cloned to
  `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project`; `/workdir/project` is a symlink to it
  created by the setup script. The fix must not move the physical clone.
- Must keep the existing pool/template provisioning, `wl sync` and prompt
  behaviour intact.
- Change is confined to the ampa plugin's `startWork` entry command; the ampa
  project is the implementation repository (see open questions).

## Existing state

- The `start-work` implementation moved out of this repository: the
  `skill/install-ampa/` skill and `ampa.mjs` plugin now live in the **ampa**
  repository (`git@github.com:SorraTheOrc/ampa.git`), under
  `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs`. It was removed from SorraAgents in
  commit `ae0d8474` ("install_ampa skill is now in the ampa proejct itself",
  2026-04-10); the `ampa-repo` git submodule pointer was also removed.
- The container setup clones to `/tmp/ampa_sandbox_<container>/project` and
  creates the symlink `/workdir/project` → that path; `/etc/ampa_bashrc` already
  ends with `cd /workdir/project`.
- Re-entry paths (`start-work` on a claimed pool container / legacy
  `ampa-<id>`) use `cd /workdir/project 2>/dev/null; … exec bash --login`.
- The initial interactive entry in `startWork` used
  `cd ${containerProjectRoot} && exec bash --login` (the `/tmp` path).
- **A fix already exists in the ampa repository on `origin/dev`**: commit
  `77856e0` ("fix: use canonical /workdir/project in start-work initial entry
  (SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW)") changes that one line to
  `cd /workdir/project && exec bash --login`. The matching branch is
  `wl-SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW-fix-start-work-directory`. It is **not yet on
  `main`** (normal dev→main release flow) and the local ampa `dev` checkout is
  one commit behind `origin/dev`.
- The fix commit contains **no automated test** and has not updated the manual
  E2E expectations.

## Desired change

Enter a freshly-provisioned dev container in the canonical
`/workdir/project` directory, matching the re-entry paths, and add regression
coverage so the initial-entry path cannot silently diverge again.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/install-ampa/resources/ampa.mjs` (ampa repository) — `startWork()`
  initial interactive entry (`distrobox enter … -c 'cd /workdir/project &&
  exec bash --login'`, currently line ~2137 on the fix branch). Also
  `buildContainerSetupScript()` / `/etc/ampa_bashrc` writer if the canonical
  path is factored out.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-devcontainer.mjs` (ampa repository) — add/extend a
  regression test for the entry command.
- `tests/node/test-ampa-start-work-template-escape.mjs` (ampa repository) —
  nearby start-work setup-script assertions if the path is interpolated.
- `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` (ampa repository) — manual E2E
  expectations / documentation of `/workdir/project`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the ampa repository, since that is where
  `start-work` lives today; the SorraAgents reference in the commit message is
  the originating work-item ID.
- **Risk:** adding an automated test may require refactoring the entry command
  out of `startWork` into a small exported helper (the command is currently
  built inline and spawned directly), otherwise it is only testable via the
  manual E2E script. Mitigation: extract a pure helper (e.g.
  `buildEntryCommand(cName)`) and unit-test it.
- **Risk:** local ampa `dev` is behind `origin/dev`; implementing from the local
  checkout without pulling would recreate/conflict with the existing fix.
  Mitigation: start from the fix branch / `origin/dev`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** while in the entry code it is tempting to refactor the
  pool/template or prompt logic. Any such extra opportunity should be recorded
  as a separate linked work item, not folded into this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MLQ8Z6V20C2FPFP** — "start-work Subcommand" (completed) — defines the
  `wl ampa start-work` behaviour this work item corrects.
- **SA-0MLQ6ZLIO1THWA9O** — "Podman development container for SorraAgents"
  (completed) — parent epic; origin of the `/workdir/project` convention.
- **SA-0MLRGE8T01IHS922** — "When run wl ampa sw do a wl sync" (completed) —
  the `wl sync` behaviour on entry/re-entry, adjacent to this flow.
- **SA-0MLQ8ZT1300Q1MOM** — "list-containers Subcommand" (completed) — related
  container lifecycle command.
- ampa repository commit `77856e0` on `origin/dev` — the existing fix.

## Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The `start-work` code now lives in the ampa repository
  (`SorraTheOrc/ampa`), and the fix for this work item is already committed
  there on `origin/dev` (`77856e0`, referencing SA-0MN7J6RO51R3TMCW), not yet on
  `main`. Should this SorraAgents work item (a) be closed as complete,
  documenting the ampa fix, (b) be migrated/copied to the ampa project's
  worklog (prefix `AM`), or (c) keep additional work in SorraAgents?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the SA implement skill runs in a
  SorraAgents worktree, where the ampa plugin no longer exists, so an
  implementer cannot make the change here without editing another repository.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The ampa fix is a one-line change with no automated
  regression test. Should this work item also add a test asserting the initial
  entry `cd`s to `/workdir/project` (which likely requires extracting the entry
  command into a testable helper), or is manual E2E coverage sufficient?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: no existing test asserts the
  entry command; `tests/manual/test-devcontainer-e2e.sh` documents the path but
  is not automated.
- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** If the fix is accepted as already complete, should the
  SorraAgents work item still record the ampa commit hash/PR and be closed once
  the fix reaches ampa `main`, or closed immediately against `origin/dev`?
  — **Answer:** *(awaiting producer)*. Context: the global workflow normally
  closes work items only after the `dev`→`main` release.

- **SA-0MN1M2B810I9YC0U** – Validate Playwright Distrobox compatibility spike (completed)
- **SA-0MPON9P8Z0062VBL** – Child work items created by /plan should start at intake_complete stage (completed)

# Audit Skill: Add Descriptive `--session-id` to Pi Subprocess Invocations

## Problem statement

The audit skill spawns `pi` subprocesses via two code paths (`audit_runner.py` and `audit_pr.py`) but does not pass `--session-id`. This means audit sessions are auto-generated UUIDs that cannot be traced back to the work item being audited, making debugging, session review, and audit traceability difficult.

## Users

- **Auditors/reviewers** — can locate the exact pi session for a given audit by WL ID
- **Operators debugging audit failures** — can inspect `PI_SESSION_ID` and find the session file
- **Maintainers of the audit skill** — can distinguish between concurrent audit runs

**Example user stories:**

- As an operator, I want the pi session created by `audit_runner.py` to carry `--session-id audit-SA-0MSABC123_phase2-abc12345` so I can find it in `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` for debugging.
- As a reviewer, I want audit sessions to be uniquely named per invocation (not per WL item) so I can see all retries and retry-specific context in their own sessions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi()` adds `--session-id audit-{issue_id}-{context}-{uuid}` to the pi command. The `context` parameter (e.g., `phase2_deep`, `parent`, `child:SA-XXX`, `verdict_reask`, `project`) is forwarded as the phase segment. The UUID is 8 hex chars (`uuid4().hex[:8]`), fresh per invocation.

2. `audit_pr.py` — `run_audit_in_worktree()` adds `--session-id audit-{wl_id}-entrypoint-{uuid}` (8 hex chars UUID, fresh per invocation). Only applied when not in `dry_run` mode.

3. The session-id format adheres to `--session-id` constraints: starts/ends with alphanumeric, contains only alphanumeric, `-`, `_`, `.` (verified by `assertValidSessionId`). Colons in context values (e.g., `child:SA-XXX`) are replaced with underscores.

4. The existing `--no-context-files --no-skills` context-reduction flags are preserved unchanged.

5. All existing tests pass, including updated mocks that verify `--session-id` is present in the command args and contains the correct WL ID.

## Constraints

- Audit skill only — no other skills spawn `pi` subprocesses.
- The session-id must not interfere with `--no-session` (if used anywhere).
- UUID must be generated at call time (per-invocation uniqueness for retry visibility).
- Must not change the command semantics — only add an additional flag.
- `audit_pr.py`: `--session-id` is only added when `dry_run=False`.

## Existing state

Two `pi` invocation sites in the audit skill:

| File | Line | Function | Phase context |
|------|------|----------|---------------|
| `audit_runner.py` | 1492 | `_call_pi()` | `context` parameter (caller supplies: `phase2_deep`, `parent`, `child:{id}`, `phase2_child:{ci}`, `phase2_batch`, `verdict_reask`, `project`) |
| `audit_pr.py` | 188 | `run_audit_in_worktree()` | Single entry point, `wl_id` parameter |

Both already pass `--no-context-files --no-skills` (SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U). Neither passes `--session-id`.

## Desired change

1. **`audit_runner.py`**: In `_call_pi()`, construct the session-id from `issue_id`, `context`, and a fresh UUID. Append `--session-id audit-<issue_id>-<context>-<uuid>` to the command before the prompt. Pass `issue_id` and `context` through `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` → `_call_pi` (already available in the call chain).

2. **`audit_pr.py`**: In `run_audit_in_worktree()`, construct session-id as `audit-{wl_id}-entrypoint-{uuid}`. Only apply when `dry_run=False`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — add `--session-id` to `_call_pi()` cmd
- `skill/audit/audit_pr.py` — add `--session-id` to `run_audit_in_worktree()` cmd
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — update mocks to verify `--session-id` in command args

## Risks & assumptions

- **Colons in context values:** `assertValidSessionId` rejects `:`. Context values like `child:SA-XXX` must be sanitized to `child_SA-XXX`.
- **Scope creep:** adding `--session-id` could interfere with `--no-session` if used anywhere. Mitigation: only add in the two known code paths.
- **Future-proofing:** future skills that spawn `pi` subprocesses will need this feature. The `assertValidSessionId` guard is in the pi core, not the audit skill.

## Related work

- SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U — audit skill context reduction (the `--no-context-files --no-skills` invariant; this work does not affect it)
- SA-0MSI51QTA009WDFO — Add session logging instruction to AGENTS.md (related: session traceability)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Format — `audit-{id}-{phase}-{uuid}` or `audit_{id}_{phase}_{uuid}`?
  A (user, 2026-08-11): `audit-{id}-{phase}-{uuid}` (dash between all segments).

- Q: Should phase be mandatory or optional?
  A (user, 2026-08-11): Only include when the code has a clear phase/step concept. If no phase, omit it entirely (don't use a placeholder).

- Q: UUID generation timing?
  A (user, 2026-08-11): Fresh per invocation — each `pi` call gets its own unique session ID, so retries appear as separate sessions.

# Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id

## Problem statement

Every pi session spawned from within a skill — the audit skill's `_call_pi()` in `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `run_audit_in_worktree()` in `audit/audit_pr.py` — is saved under pi's default random session ID, so when debugging an audit run it is impossible to tell which session belongs to which work item or which phase produced it. Skills should pass `--session-id` so every spawned pi session clearly identifies the work item it is for and the action being taken (e.g. `audit-{id}-{phase}-{uuid}`).

## Users

- **Producers/operators** debugging audit runs: want to identify, resume, and inspect the exact pi session for a given work item and phase (`pi --session <id>` / `/resume`).
- **Audit skill maintainers**: want session-per-call isolation (unique ID per call) so parallel/fan-out pi calls never share a session file and never re-trigger the "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" failure mode.
- **Operators of long-running systems**: want stale skill-spawned sessions pruned automatically so `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` does not grow unboundedly.

### Example user stories

- As a producer, I want each pi session spawned during an audit to carry `--session-id audit-{work_item_id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}`, so I can resume the exact session that produced a failed verdict.
- As a maintainer, I want each call to get a unique session (not a shared one), so repeated calls never append into the same session file and never hit the assistant-role continuation error that Ralph's original `--no-session` fix addressed.
- As an operator, I want `audit-*` sessions older than a retention period automatically pruned after each audit run, so the session store stays bounded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every pi subprocess spawned by the audit skill passes `--session-id` with a unique per-call value. `_call_pi()` in `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` appends `--session-id <id>` to the constructed command; the value is generated in `_call_pi_and_maybe_log()` as `audit-{work_item_id}-{context}-{short_uuid}` (short uuid = `uuid4().hex[:8]`).
- [ ] `audit/audit_pr.py` `run_audit_in_worktree()` passes `--session-id audit-pr-{wl_id}-{short_uuid}` for each spawned pi call.
- [ ] Session IDs are unique per call — no two calls share a session file; session-per-call isolation means no "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" errors are introduced.
- [ ] Project-level audits (no work-item id) use a stable placeholder in the id (`audit-project-{short_uuid}` — dedupe the repeated `project` context so the id reads cleanly).
- [ ] Automatic cleanup runs at the end of an audit run (`issue` and `project` commands): session files whose names match the `audit-` prefix and whose mtime is older than the retention period (default 112 days) are pruned from the pi session directory.
- [ ] Retention is configurable via a `--session-retention-days` CLI flag on both subcommands and/or an `AUDIT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` env var (flag wins).
- [ ] Cleanup is conservative: it only removes `audit-`-prefixed sessions — never other pi sessions.
- [ ] Tests verify: (a) `--session-id` appears in every constructed pi command with the expected format, (b) session ids are unique across calls, (c) cleanup prunes only stale `audit-*` files and honors the retention setting, (d) existing cmd-construction tests (e.g. `TestCallPiEnableTools`) are updated and still pass.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the established Ralph session-per-call precedent (SA-0MQ6E8NCG003STJB): unique `--session-id` per call, dash-separated `{skill}-{work_item_id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}` format, conservative prefix-scoped cleanup, default retention 112 days.
- Backward compatible: `_call_pi()` gains an optional `session_id: str | None = None` parameter; when unset the command is byte-identical to today (existing direct callers/tests unaffected).
- Cleanup must never touch sessions that do not start with the `audit-` prefix.
- The audit skill's context-reduction invariants (`--no-context-files --no-skills`, self-contained prompts) are untouched.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (managed by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` `_call_pi()` (line ~1492): `cmd = [pi_bin, "-p", "--mode", "json", "--model", model, prompt]` (+ optional `--tools`, always `--no-context-files --no-skills`). Sessions are saved under pi's default random IDs.
- `_call_pi_and_maybe_log(issue_id, context, prompt, ...)` (line ~2816) already threads `issue_id` (a work-item id, a child id, or `"project"`) and `context` (e.g. `parent`, `phase2_deep`, `child_ac_fallback`) for debug-log naming, but does not forward them to `_call_pi()`.
- `audit/audit_pr.py` `run_audit_in_worktree()` (line ~192): `cmd = ['pi', '-p', '--mode', 'json', f"/audit {wl_id}"]` — `wl_id` is in scope.
- No `--session-id` usage exists anywhere in the skill tree today.
- Session storage: pi saves to `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<path-slug>--/` (overridable via `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` / `--session-dir`); cleanup should honor the env/flag override when present.

# Pane title status indicator on skill completion

## Problem statement

When a skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, …) finishes, the operator
cannot tell at a glance whether the pane's work-item session ended cleanly,
needs their attention, or failed. The herdr pane title currently shows only
the dispatch context (e.g. `Manually triggered intake`); the end-of-session
state must be surfaced in the pane title itself.

## Users

- **Operator (producer)** watching a grid of herdr panes: wants a zero-click
  visual signal of which sessions are done, need attention, or failed —
  without opening each pane.

Example user stories:

- "As an operator, when a skill completes cleanly I want a green tick at the
  start of the pane title so I can see it finished."
- "As an operator, when a skill completes but left information for my
  attention I want an orange warning so I know to look at it."
- "As an operator, when a skill cannot complete I want a red no-entry sign
  so I know to intervene."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When a work-item skill finishes and produces a final report, the herdr
  pane title (label) for the current pane is updated with a status prefix:
  ✅ (or `Done`) when all ACs are met and no substantive producer content
  exists; ⚠️ (or `Note`) when the skill completed but the report contains
  substantive content for the producer's attention; 🚫 (or `Attention`) when
  the skill cannot complete (any unmet/partial/adjusted AC verdict, or
  abort/failure).
- AC2: The prefix is prepended to the existing pane title (e.g.
  `✅ Manually triggered intake`); no colour/ANSI is embedded in the label;
  the update is idempotent (re-running does not stack prefixes).
- AC3: Text fallbacks `Done` / `Note` / `Attention` are used when emoticons
  are not possible (reusing the report's existing `--no-icons` /
  `WL_NO_ICONS=1` mechanism).
- AC4: On skill abort or failure (including abort paths such as
  `intake.py abort`, `implement.py abort`, audit-runner aborts), the pane
  title is set to the red state regardless of whether a final report is
  produced.
- AC5: The update fails gracefully outside a herdr pane (no `HERDR_ENV`,
  `HERDR_PANE_ID`, or herdr CLI unavailable): no crash, no error surfaced to
  the skill run.
- AC6: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and all
  related documentation is updated (SKILL.md reports, tests for the new
  helper).

## Constraints

- Not a pi extension — the update is a call to the herdr CLI/API
  (`herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>`; current pane id from
  `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var; herdr ≥ current installed version).
- Trigger is skill completion (end-of-session report render), not the agent
  harness lifecycle.
- Status is derived from the final report's content: AC verdicts
  (met/unmet/adjusted/partial), Producer Actions, Notes.
- Orange = "audit passed but there is information for the producer's
  attention (not necessarily actions, and certainly not when the next action
  is the standard next action in the workflow)" — i.e. substantive content
  beyond the routine workflow next step.
- Colour requirement dropped for text fallbacks: plain `Done`/`Note`/
  `Attention` prefixes, no colour coding.
- Emoji-vs-text fallback follows the existing report convention
  (`--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1`), so both modes stay consistent.

## Existing state

- Every work-item skill ends by rendering a canonical report via
  `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (report skill, SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S),
  passing AC verdicts, producer actions, notes and next action.
- herdr panes carry a `label` field shown as the pane title, set via
  `herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>`; current pane is identified by the
  `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var (present in pi sessions launched via herdr; also
  `HERDR_ENV=1` and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`).
- `render_report.py` already supports `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` for
  bracketed-text fallbacks — a precedent for the emoticon/text switch.

## Desired change

- Add a small shared helper (e.g. `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`) that, given a
  status (`done` | `note` | `attention`) and the current pane context,
  prepends the corresponding prefix (✅/⚠️/🚫 or Done/Note/Attention) to the
  existing pane label via the herdr CLI, idempotently.
- Integrate the helper into `render_report.py`: after the report is rendered,
  derive the status from the supplied AC verdicts, producer actions and notes
  and update the pane title (done/note states; red when any AC verdict is not
  met).
- Hook the red state into abort paths (`intake.py abort`, `implement.py
  abort`, audit runner abort/exit paths) so failures always surface red even
  without a final report.
- Fail open when not in a herdr pane or herdr CLI is missing.

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — derive status from report inputs
  and call the pane-title helper after rendering.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` (new) — shared herdr CLI wrapper: resolve
  current pane, read existing label, prepend status prefix idempotently.
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — abort command sets red pane state.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — abort path sets red pane state.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — abort/failure exits set red pane
  state.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` + `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` —
  document and test the status derivation and pane update.

## Risks & assumptions

- **herdr CLI availability:** assume herdr is installed and the pane env vars
  are set in agent panes (true today — pi sessions launched via herdr carry
  `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`). Fail-open behaviour (AC5) mitigates drift.
- **Existing pane title truncation:** herdr truncates long labels to ~60
  chars (`MAX_PANE_TITLE_LENGTH`); the prefix plus existing label must fit
  within the limit — the helper should truncate the combined string the same
  way to keep the title valid.
- **Scope creep:** wiring red-state into *every* skill's abort path is broad;
  the helper centralises the logic so each abort site is a one-liner. Extra
  opportunities (e.g. coloured labels in the herdr UI itself) are recorded as
  follow-up work items, not scope.
- **Verdict vocabulary:** `adjusted`/`partial` verdicts count as "not fully
  met" → red; `met` only → eligible for done/note.

## Related work

- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill": the report renderer this feature extends.
- ContextHub herdr (sibling repo `packages/herdr`): `pane rename`, pane
  titles (`pane-title.ts`, WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), agent-state protocol.
- find-related matches (repo): `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — the
  abort/failure paths that must surface the red state; no directly-related
  open work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should this live in the SorraAgents repo as a reusable extension, or be a built-in feature in the pi-coding-agent?" — Answer (user): "It is not a pi extension, it is a call to the herdr CLI/API." Source: interactive reply (intake session).
- Q: "Should the title update happen on agent_settled or agent_end?" — Answer (user): "Triggers by the completion of a skill, not by the agent harness." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "To detect a producer notification, check needsProducerReview?" — Answer (user): "The final summary from the skill indicates status." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What should the complete title look like?" — Answer (user): "Just add the prefix to the existing title." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Which herdr command sets the pane title?" — Answer (user): "Don't know — look it up using herdr --help." Research: `herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>` sets the pane label (pane list `label` field, e.g. `Manually triggered intake`); current pane id from `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var; `herdr pane report-metadata --title` is display-only metadata (not the label). Accepted answer: `herdr pane rename` with `HERDR_PANE_ID`.
- Q: "Status derivation from the final summary?" — Answer (user): "Green is correct; Orange is audit passed but there is information for the producer's attention (not necessarily actions, and certainly not when the next action is the standard next action in the workflow); Red is correct." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Where should the herdr call live?" — Answer (user): "(a) inside render_report.py so every skill gets it automatically." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Orange trigger precision — substantive content?" — Answer (user): "Substantive content." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Red path for aborts?" — Answer (user): "Always show red." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Fallback colour mechanics?" — Answer (user): "Drop the colour requirement." Source: interactive reply.

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher gates implement dispatch on `open/plan_complete` items having `risk ≤ Medium` and `effort ≤ Medium` (`classifyItemForDispatch` fails closed when risk/effort are absent). Items created without estimates are therefore **never implement-dispatchable** and no mechanism evaluates them (evidence: open_source_llm has 6 of 7 open plan_complete items with empty risk/effort — OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA et al.). The ContextHub dispatcher-side fix (P4) will either dispatch a risk/effort evaluation or adopt a default; either way the **implement skill** must behave correctly when invoked on (or alongside) an item whose estimates are missing — currently the effort/risk gate blocks the run instead of producing the missing data.

When starting implementation of a plan_complete item that lacks risk and/or effort, run the risk/effort evaluation (the effort-and-risk skill — `skill/effort-and-risk`/`effort_and_risk_skill`) **before/at gate time** and persist the estimates on the work item (wl update --risk/--effort), so the item is properly sized and the run proceeds — rather than failing on the gate.

1. Invoking implement on a plan_complete item with empty risk/effort produces and persists risk/effort estimates and proceeds (or cleanly hands off to the evaluation), instead of refusing on the gate.

The end-of-session report helper (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) always renders **Audit: ❔ not run** in the Meta-Data block, even when the work item has a persisted, passing audit.

### Root cause

`wl show <id> --json` returns `auditResult` as a **top-level** key of the response envelope:

```json
{ "success": true, "workItem": { ... }, "auditResult": { "readyToClose": true, ... }, "comments": [...] }
```

`render_metadata()` reads `work_item.get("auditResult")` (line ~235), where `work_item = data.get("workItem", {})` — the top-level `auditResult` is never consulted, so the lookup is always falsy and the audit status degrades to "not run".

Discovered while rendering the final report for SA-0MU7FD0YF0065EG9, whose audit had passed (`readyToClose: true`, all 4 ACs met) yet the report showed "Audit: not run".

### Acceptance Criteria

1. `render_metadata()` resolves audit status from the top-level `auditResult` of the `wl show --json` envelope (falling back to any `workItem.auditResult` for backward compatibility), so a `readyToClose: true` result renders as passed and `readyToClose: false` renders as failed.
2. A unit test covers: top-level `auditResult` with `readyToClose: true` → "passed"; `readyToClose: false` → "failed"; absent/null → "not run".
3. `--json` (stdin) mode continues to work for callers that pass a bare work-item dict.

## Problem Statement

Agents repeatedly make the same mistakes when working with pi — using `skill_path` as a bash command instead of the tool, expanding backticks in shell commands, forgetting Python imports, and falling into self-correction loops. A skill that analyses recent session logs to detect these patterns would enable proactive skill improvements and prevent recurring failures.

## Users

- **Agent operator / PI** — receives a structured report of agent confusion patterns and actionable improvement recommendations.
- **Skill authors** — get targeted work items to update SKILL.md files, scripts, or add guardrails.
- **Producers** — understand systemic agent behaviour issues across the project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Skill reads the last 20 session logs (`.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl`) for the CWD project, sorted by modification time.
2. Heuristic analysis extracts: tool call distribution, thinking-content error signals (keywords: error, fail, retry, incorrect, sorry, wrong, fix, correct, issue, problem, confused, wait, actually, oh, hmm, ah), tool result errors (tracebacks, permission denied, command not found, shell expansion errors), and retry/self-correction patterns.
3. LLM-assisted interpretation (via pi calls) classifies patterns into categories (e.g. "skill invocation confusion", "shell quoting issues", "Python import omissions", "permission issues") and generates recommendations.
4. Structured report rendered in the agent response with: summary of findings, top patterns by frequency, recommended skill improvements, and evidence citations (which sessions showed which patterns).
5. Recommendations are filed as worklog comments on the parent work item.
6. For each actionable recommendation, a child work item is auto-created with issue-type `chore` or `feature`, assigned to Map, and linked via `related-to:<parent-id>` in the description.
7. The skill follows existing project conventions: `skill/agent-log-review/SKILL.md`, `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/`, `skill/agent-log-review/tests/`.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (e.g. `docs/dev/agent-log-review-skill-reference.md`).
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Hybrid approach: heuristics for extraction, LLM for classification — not fully automated LLM-only (too expensive) and not heuristic-only (too noisy).
- Only CWD project sessions; no cross-project analysis.
- Auto-create work items but don't implement them — that's downstream work.
- Must handle v3 session log format (session, model_change, thinking_level_change, message types with content as list of thinking/toolCall parts).

# tree_coverage truncates wrapped AC bullets

## Discovery

Found while planning SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63: the AC-coverage review reported `coverage_pct: 0.0`
and `recommendation: stop` even though every parent AC is genuinely covered by a child. Root
cause: `extract_acceptance_criteria()` in `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` captures only the first
physical line of each `- ` bullet. Work-item descriptions wrap their AC bullets (as the global
`AGENTS.md`/intake/plan conventions produce), so the parent ACs handed to the Jaccard matcher are
truncated mid-sentence:

```
'**AC1 — Hermetic git usage:** every test helper that runs real `git` commands'
```

instead of the full criterion. The child ACs are truncated the same way, and the resulting
similarity scores (0.14-0.28) fall below the 0.4 threshold, producing a false `stop` that blocks
`plan_complete`. This is also consistent with the earlier observation recorded on
SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 that keeping an auxiliary item as a `wl` child made coverage report `stop`.

## Goal

Wrapped acceptance-criteria bullets are extracted whole, so the coverage review measures real
coverage rather than first-line snippets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** `extract_acceptance_criteria()` joins continuation lines of a wrapped `- ` bullet until
  the next blank line, next bullet, or next `##` heading, and returns the full criterion text.
  *Verification:* a unit test with a multi-line wrapped AC asserts the full text is returned.
- **AC2** A regression test reproduces the observed failure: a parent with wrapped ACs and a child
  whose mapping bullet restates the *full* parent AC yields `fully_covered: True`; and the
  pre-fix behaviour (first-line-only) is covered by an explicit test asserting the fix (not by
  asserting the bug).
- **AC3** Backwards compatibility: descriptions whose ACs are already single-line return identical
  results (`skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` stays green, extended as needed).
- **AC4** The similarity threshold semantics are documented in the module docstring: tokens are
  lowercased/punctuation-stripped, and parent/child AC text is compared as whole criteria.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` — `extract_acceptance_criteria`, `compute_coverage`, `resolve_coverage_gaps`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py` — regression tests.
- `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md` — note the mapping convention (child ACs should restate the
  parent criterion they cover).

## Notes

- Discovered during planning of SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63. Workaround applied in that plan: each child
  carries an explicit `Covers parent ACn — ...` bullet restating the parent AC's first line, which
  lifts the Jaccard score to ~0.8 and lets the review return `proceed` (100%).
- A real fix should not require the workaround wording.

- **discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63

Discovered during the find-related v3 review (discovered-from:SA-0MNCDAQ8W008KOG9).

The v3 overhaul reduced search subprocesses from 523 to 8 and wall-clock from a 240s+ timeout to ~3s on the *measurement machine*. Re-measured on a typical development machine, wall-clock is **~5-6s**, which exceeds the skill's documented <5s expectation.

- [ ] SKILL.md runtime expectations match the measured figure

Keyword extraction is frequency-ranked and capped to the top 8 (`MAX_SEARCH_KEYWORDS`), but the highest-frequency terms are generic words, so the search returns weakly related items.

- Preserve the v3 feedback-loop fix (report section stripped before extraction; no unbounded keyword growth).
- Conservative policy: prefer false negatives over false positives.

# implement.py finish leaves local dev behind after pushing to remote dev

Counterpart of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB**
(`discovered-from:AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB`). The defect is in agent infrastructure in this
repository — `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`. The full discovery context (observed
commits, parent run, workaround) is on the AI_Hell report; this item is the actionable fix.

## Headline

After `implement.py finish <child>` pushes the child's branch to `origin/dev`, the main
checkout's local `dev` branch is left one or more commits behind, so the next
`implement.py parent <epic>` / `implement.py start <child>` creates the following child's
worktree from a stale base and is missing the previous sibling's files.

## Problem statement

`phase_finish` restores the main checkout to the parent branch **before** pushing the
just-committed branch to `origin dev`:

- Step 7 — `_restore_repo_state(repo_root)` runs `git checkout dev` then `git pull origin dev`
  (local `dev` fast-forwards only to the **pre-push** remote tip).
- Step 8 — `git_push_to_dev(repo_root, branch)` runs
  `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` (the new commit lands on the remote after the pull).

Local `dev` is therefore left behind. `git_worktree_add()` forks each child from the **local**
parent branch (`git worktree add --track -b <branch> <worktree> dev`) and `phase_start`
performs no fetch, so every subsequent child starts from the stale base.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running the parent/epic flow (`implement.py parent`).
- **Operators / orchestrators** relying on the parent flow being self-consistent without
  manual `git fetch` / `git merge` steps.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, after `finish` reports "commit pushed to dev", I want the main
  checkout's local `dev` to contain that commit, so the next `parent`/`start` child worktree
  includes my just-finished sibling's files.
- As an operator, I want the parent flow to never create a child from a stale base, so I do
  not have to diagnose phantom build errors or risk lost/duplicated work.

## Observed (from AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB)

- F2 (`AH-0MUBYU600004YU4T`) `finish` pushed `91538d0` to `origin/dev`; local `dev` stayed at
  `1920e65`.
- The F3 worktree (`AH-0MUBYXR280018HST`) was created from local `dev` `1920e65` and could not
  resolve `../powerups/collectAnimation` (added by F2) until local `dev` was manually
  fast-forwarded and merged into the worktree.
- Workaround applied by hand during the parent `AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W` run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Post-push local parent sync.** After a successful push in `phase_finish`, the
  main checkout's local parent branch (`dev`) is at least as advanced as the pushed tip when
  it is safe to fast-forward (local `dev` == pushed commit == `origin/dev`).
- [ ] **AC2 — Safe-skip semantics.** When the update is not safe (dirty main checkout, other
  branch/detached, or local `dev` diverged), `finish` does not force it, loses no local
  commits, and does not fail. The skip is reported and the repo remains recoverable.
- [ ] **AC3 — Children never start from a stale base.** `parent`/`start` refresh the parent
  branch (`fetch` + fast-forward) before `git worktree add`, or fork from
  `origin/<parent_branch>` after a fetch.
- [ ] **AC4 — Regression tests.** A focused regression test (e.g.
  `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py`) covers AC1–AC3; existing
  `tests/test_implement_*.py` still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation updated** (`skill/implement/SKILL.md`, code comments, README and
  any relevant docs-site entries) for the new post-push sync and safe-skip semantics.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies; reuse stdlib and the existing `run_cmd` / `git_*` helpers.
- Never force-update a branch with local commits; prefer `--ff-only`.
- Must not regress worktree-based finish (worktree is removed before the push).
- Remote-unreachable / dirty-checkout paths degrade gracefully (report, do not fail a finish
  that already pushed successfully).
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_PARENT_BRANCH = "dev"`.
- `_restore_repo_state(repo_root)` → `git checkout dev`; `git pull origin dev`.
- `git_push_to_dev(cwd, branch)` → `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev`.
- `git_worktree_add(branch, worktree_path, parent_branch)` → `git worktree add --track -b ...`;
  `phase_start` does no fetch.
- `phase_finish` order: remove worktree → `_restore_repo_state` → `git_push_to_dev`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — reorder/guard the post-push local parent sync and
  refresh the parent branch in `phase_start` before `git_worktree_add`.
- `tests/test_implement_finish_local_parent_branch.py` — new regression test for AC1–AC3.
- `tests/test_implement_parent_recursion.py`, `tests/test_implement_parent_safety.py` —
  extend parent-flow coverage (fresh base for the next child).
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — document the post-push local parent sync and safe-skip semantics.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB** — AI_Hell discovery report (this item's origin).
- **AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W** — AI_Hell parent epic where the stale base was observed.
- **SA-0MT9607Q5009JA2V** — precedent AI_Hell→SorraAgents counterpart pattern.
- **SA-0MQP8K03I007DVMM** — prior worktree-awareness work in the implement flow.
- **SA-0MSIVM00X003E5PZ**, **SA-0MSI8YLTN0007KN8** — other `phase_finish` robustness fixes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** auto-updating local `dev` could clobber intentional local commits — mitigate with a
  clean/on-branch/no-divergence guard and `--ff-only`.
- **Risk:** `git pull`/`fetch` in a dirty or offline main checkout — never fail a finish that
  already pushed.
- **Risk (scope creep):** a generic "sync all worktrees" mechanism or changing the
  push-to-`dev` policy are out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which repository owns the fix?** — **Answer (agent research):** SorraAgents (this repo).
  Evidence: `implement.py` lives here and the global skill is a symlink into this repo; AI_Hell
  contains no `implement.py`.
- **Q: Is the bug still present?** — **Answer (agent research):** yes, `_restore_repo_state`
  runs before `git_push_to_dev` in `phase_finish`.

## Problem
The main checkout has a stale LOCAL branch literally named `origin/dev` (`refs/heads/origin/dev`), separate from the remote-tracking ref `refs/remotes/origin/dev`. Git treats the unqualified name `origin/dev` as ambiguous (warning) and resolves it to the local branch.

- Clean up accidental local branches that shadow remote-tracking refs (operator decision — do not delete without permission).
- Harden ref resolution to prefer fully-qualified `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` (the SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 sync helper already does this) and/or detect the ambiguous-ref warning.

# Problem statement

The audit runner's parent-first flow re-audits all children on every run because the freshness fingerprint includes the global git HEAD sha. In `--child-in-main-slot` mode, non-interactive runs leave all children with `partial` verdicts, which blocks the parent from recording a "Ready to close: Yes" result even when all parent ACs are met. This prevents audit completion for epics whose children were previously audited.

# Users

- **Audit runner / downtime worker** — expects a non-interactive audit of an epic to produce a valid verdict without requiring a live agent session.
- **Producer / human reviewer** — expects the audit to accurately reflect whether work is ready to close, not to block on stale or unserviced child verdicts.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fingerprint scoping.** `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger; instead it is scoped to child-relevant key files and/or commits so that unrelated HEAD movement on `dev` does not invalidate previously valid child audits.
- **AC2 — In-main-slot partial verdict handling.** When a child's `ac_results` remain `partial` because the invoking agent session never serviced the `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items, the parent audit treats those verdicts as "not assessed" (inherits the child's previously stored verdict or marks them reusable) rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic clarity.** The audit output surfaces a clear, machine-parseable diagnostic that distinguishes a "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" verdict from a genuine "not-ready" child verdict, including the reason code in the audit summary.
- **AC4 — No regression on interactive runs.** The above fixes do not change the behaviour of interactive audit runs (where an agent session *can* service in-main-slot items); those continue to honour the full in-main-slot workflow.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite and confirm zero failures.

# Constraints

- The fix must not introduce a new mode flag or require operator configuration; it should be the default behaviour.
- The fix should be backward-compatible with persisted audit results (old fingerprint format should still be readable).
- The change scope is the audit runner's child freshness logic (`_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`), the in-main-slot verdict accumulation logic (`_build_issue_json`, `all_ac_acceptable`), and the diagnostic output path.

# Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` includes the current git HEAD sha — any new commit on `dev` invalidates every stored child audit.
- In `child_in_main_slot=True` mode, child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking session. In non-interactive runs, these are never serviced and stay `partial`.
- `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect.

# Desired change

1. **Scope the fingerprint**: Replace the global HEAD sha in `_compute_content_fingerprint` with a child-scoped hash (key files + relevant commits).
2. **Handle partial verdicts**: When computing `all_ac_acceptable`, skip children whose verdict is `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot items — treat them as "not assessed" rather than "not accepted."
3. **Add diagnostics**: In the audit summary, emit a reason code or flag indicating when a child's `partial` verdict is due to unserviced in-main-slot items vs. genuine assessment failure.

# Key Files (predicted)

## Summary

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out (many concurrent `audit_runner.py issue OSL-*` processes) ran the test suite with a **leaked `GIT_DIR`** pointing at a live worktree's git dir. Tests that use real `git` (git init/commit/push fixtures) therefore operated on the **live repository** instead of their temp dirs: they committed 24 junk commits (`init`/`Initial commit`, authors `Test <test@test.com>`, `T <t@t>`, `Cache Test`, `RT Test`) on top of the then-current `dev` tip and **pushed them to `origin/dev`**, gutting the branch (483 files, -144,702 lines).

This is the exact incident class documented in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (2026-09-24 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident, SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 / docs/dev/test-isolation.md) — the sandbox helper neutralises the vars for test fixtures, but the **production test-execution path does not**.

## Evidence

- Orphaned (`PPID 1`) `audit_runner.py issue OSL-*` processes with env:
  `GIT_DIR=/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.git/worktrees/wl-OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT-nested-node-modules`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core`, `GIT_PREFIX=`.
- Their `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings` children inherited the same `GIT_DIR`.
- `refs/heads/dev` reflog: last legitimate entry `763b8f11` (push by Sorra the Orc), then 24 test commits by `T/Test/Cache Test/RT Test`.
- `refs/heads/dev` and the shared `.git/config` (`core.bare=true`) were rewritten; `.git/HEAD` moved to junk.
- `git ls-remote origin dev` showed the junk tip `6366f913` (fast-forward from `763b8f11`, so the push was accepted).

## Impact

- `origin/dev` overwritten (recovered to `763b8f11` via `--force-with-lease` by the implement session).
- Shared main checkout `core.bare=true`, `dev` ref clobbered (recovered).
- Collateral: another agent's uncommitted work in the main checkout was reset/lost.
- Any push/CI consuming `dev` during the window would have seen the gutted tree.

## Root cause / propagation

- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner` does `env = os.environ.copy()` and passes it to `subprocess.run` **without stripping `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS`**. `GIT_DIR` overrides `cwd` for every git subprocess, so fixture `git init/commit/push` hit the live repo.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_run_tests_via_test_skill` -> `run_cached`) have the same gap.
- The origin of the leaked `GIT_DIR` in the launcher is external to `skill/` (no setter found in the repo); the audit fan-out was orphaned. **Defence-in-depth must not depend on the launcher being clean.**

## Proposed fix

1. Scrub `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` (from `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`) in `test_cache._default_runner` (and any other subprocess that runs tests) before spawning — single choke point.
2. `run_tests.py`: strip the same vars in its runner/env.
3. `audit_runner.py`: strip before `run_cached`/`run_tests`; ensure per-item audits cannot fan out unbounded (34+ concurrent observed).
4. Regression test: with `GIT_DIR` set to the live repo in `os.environ`, a fixture `git init/commit` must NOT touch  the live checkout (extend `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`).
5. Consider making the live-repo guard fail-fast (abort the run) rather than only post-hoc, and have `run_tests.py` refuse to run when `GIT_DIR`/override vars are present.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test_cache._default_runner` (and `run_tests.py`/`audit_runner.py`) remove `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_CONFIG*`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` before spawning tests.
- [ ] Regression test reproduces the leak (fixture mutation under a poisoned `GIT_DIR`) and proves the scrub prevents it.
- [ ] `origin/dev` cannot be moved by any test fixture (asserted).
- [ ] Audit fan-out is bounded (`AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_AUDITS` honoured; no 30+ concurrent orphans).
- [ ] Full suite green.

# audit_runner failure-restore reuses an invalid pre-audit status/stage combo, leaving items unrecoverable

## Problem statement

When an audit ends in an infrastructure-failure / fallback-tainted "Ready to close: No" verdict, `audit_runner.py` restores the captured pre-audit `status`+`stage` verbatim. If that captured combination is already invalid (which happens when an item was imported/refiled with status and stage set independently), every restore attempt is rejected by `wl` and the item is left in an unresolved, inconsistent state.

Observed during the audit of SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD on 2026-09-26 (session herdr-1790437388-2668941-15858, log `/home/rgardler/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD-20260926-173301.log`):

- Phase 1 parent screening hit audit-concurrency starvation → unparseable → infra-fallback `partial` for all ACs.
- `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` correctly chose the restore branch, building `wl update <id> --status blocked --stage in_review`.
- The captured combo was invalid (`blocked` is not compatible with `in_review`), so all 3 attempts failed.
- The runner printed "the item's lifecycle is unresolved" and exited non-zero.

The item's pre-audit status was already invalid (`in-progress`/`in_review`; `wl` allows stage `in_review` only with status `completed`).

## Root cause

`_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (~L10960) and `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` (~L10828) only substitute a safe stage when `safe_stage` is falsy (i.e. `ctx.original_stage` was never captured). A present-but-invalid captured combo is used as-is, so the restore cannot succeed and the item is stranded.

## Desired change

Before applying a restore (or a "No" demotion), validate the intended `(status, stage)` pair against `wl`'s allowed combinations and coerce to the nearest valid pair (e.g. keep the status but fall back to `plan_complete`/`intake_complete`/`idea` for non-completed statuses), or retry with a stage-agnostic update. Never leave an item in an invalid combination after the runner exits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the captured pre-audit `(status, stage)` combination is invalid, the failure/restore path applies a valid, consistent state instead of failing all attempts, and the runner never leaves the item in an invalid combination.
2. A regression test covers restoring an item whose captured combo is invalid (e.g. `blocked`/`in_review`) and asserts a valid terminal state is reached.
3. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
4. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The fix must not alter the semantic intent of the restore: preserve the captured status (e.g. `blocked` stays `blocked`) and only coerce the stage when the combination is invalid.
- The valid status/stage mapping is defined in `config.js` (`statusStageCompatibility`):
  - `open` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `in-progress` → `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `input_needed` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `blocked` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`
  - `completed` → `in_review`, `done`
  - `deleted` → `idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `done`
- The fix should be self-contained in the audit runner's restore logic; no changes to `wl` itself.

## Existing state

Two locations apply the restore:
1. `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` (~L10828) — standalone restore after verification failure.
2. `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (~L10960) — primary restore path in the verdict-driven transition.

Both follow the same pattern:
```python
safe_status = ctx.original_status or "open"
safe_stage = ctx.original_stage
if not safe_stage:
    safe_stage = "in_review" if safe_status == "completed" else "plan_complete"
```

This only handles the case where `original_stage` was never captured. When `original_stage` exists but is incompatible with `original_status`, the combo is invalid and rejected by `wl`.

## Desired change (implementation)

Introduce a helper function `_coerce_valid_status_stage(status, stage)` that:
1. Validates the `(status, stage)` pair against the `statusStageCompatibility` map.
2. Returns `(status, stage)` unchanged if valid.
3. If invalid, keeps the captured status but falls back to a valid stage:
   - For non-`completed` statuses: `plan_complete` (the closest "work in progress" stage).
   - For `completed`: `in_review`.
4. Logs a warning when coercion occurs, so operators know the original state was non-standard.

Apply this helper in both `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` and `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` before building the `wl update` command.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Coercion changes the restored state slightly.** The stage may shift (e.g. `in_review` → `plan_complete` for a `blocked` item). This is intentional and safer than leaving the item unrecoverable. Operators should note the warning message.
- **The `statusStageCompatibility` mapping lives in ContextHub's `config.js`, not SorraAgents.** The audit runner must not import from ContextHub. Valid combos should be inlined in `audit_runner.py` (or sourced from a shared constant in `skill/shared/`). This is a deliberate isolation choice.
- **Scope creep risk:** Only fix the restore path — do not address all status/stage issues in the runner (e.g. the "No" demotion path or the "Yes" advance path, which already produce valid combos). Source: explicit scope from the original report.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSG9SLGI002OF7V** — "Audit runner demotes in_review item to open/plan_complete on infrastructure-failure fallback verdicts" — the prior fix that added the `fallback_tainted` flag and restore path. This issue is a follow-up: the restore itself fails when the captured combo is invalid.
- **SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD** — the item that exposed the bug during audit.
- **SA-0MS99053T001ED0C** — "find-related and refactor skills still flip status to completed via StatusLifecycle" — related StatusLifecycle correctness issue.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** When coercing an invalid `(status, stage)` pair, should we preserve the captured status or also attempt to adjust the status? — **Answer (Map):** Preserve the captured status and only coerce the stage. The status carries the item's operational state (blocked/in-progress/open) which should not be silently altered. Source: analysis of the `statusStageCompatibility` mapping.
- **Q2:** Should the coercion helper be placed in `audit_runner.py` or shared (`status_lifecycle.py`)? — **Answer (Map):** Place it in `audit_runner.py` for now; if `status_lifecycle.py` needs the same logic (e.g. for general wl validation), refactor to shared later. Source: current usage is audit-runner-specific.
- **Q3:** What log level should coercion warnings use? — **Answer (Map):** `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` (consistent with existing error paths in the runner). Source: audit_runner.py convention.

# Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`

Refiled from ContextHub (originally WL-0MUJKDX93000BJB4, now deleted there) — the defect is in SorraAgents' ship skill (`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`), so it is tracked here.

Discovered while investigating why the ContextHub v1.0.16 release auto-closed **0 of 14** released `in_review` items.

## Problem

`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` refuses to `wl close --force <parent>` whenever **any** descendant is not itself in the close-candidate set. The candidate set is built from `getCandidateItems()` (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`), which returns **only** `stage: in_review` items.

Descendants already terminal (`stage: done`) are therefore *not* candidates, so they are classified as "collateral" and the parent close is refused — even though a done child needs no action and re-affirming it is harmless.

## Evidence (ContextHub v1.0.16)

11 parents refused; their combined descendants classified:

- **29 already `stage: done`** → false-positive collateral (the defect)
- **1 `stage: in_review` with `needsProducerReview=true`** → legitimately skipped, but also counted as collateral
- **18 open/blocked non-terminal** (`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`) → refusal is correct (force-close must not sweep unfinished work)

Per parent:

| Parent (ContextHub WL id) | done children | non-terminal children | Refusal valid? |
|---|---|---|---|
| WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V | 9 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MSLW8GHQ0092PJK | 5 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q | 4 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514 | 3 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MSOYWZTH003JFVD | 3 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 | 1 | 0 | no — false positive |
| WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI | 1 | 4 | yes |
| WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28 | 3 | 2 | yes (includes npr=true child) |
| WL-0MU6UL0RJ008IHGT | 0 | 1 | yes |
| WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 | 0 | 7 | yes |
| WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW | 0 | 5 | yes |

## Desired behaviour

1. The collateral-exclusion set must exclude descendants already terminal (`stage: done`), so a parent whose only non-candidate descendants are done is closable.
2. A descendant skipped solely because `needsProducerReview=true` should block the parent explicitly (reported as such), not be lumped under "collateral".
3. Genuine non-terminal descendants (`open`/`blocked`/`in_progress`) must still block the parent close.
4. Regression tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn` cover: (a) all-done descendants → parent closes; (b) one non-terminal descendant → parent refused; (c) npr=true descendant → parent refused with a distinct reason.
5. `npm run build` and existing suites pass.

## Notes

- Parents in the "refusal valid" rows were advanced to `in_review` while children remain open/blocked — a separate tracking-hygiene concern; possibly related to SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0 (audit runner `inherited_pass` bypasses the children-stage block).
- Related: SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H (parent-coverage / out-of-scope rules for child audits), SA-0MSAL2NQV0008HY5.

Switch this clone (and any other drifted clones) to `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` so the committed v3 hook runs.
